title: Granular outlier suppression and adaptive layer-scaling for cross-model quant profiles
creator: Asha Patel
description: Implement a per-layer, head-aware outlier suppression and adaptive scaling mechanism to stabilize FP8/INT8 calibration across LLama, Mistral, and Qwen families. This ticket unblocks a general-purpose calibration pipeline that reduces post-quantization accuracy regressions observed in recent smoke tests, particularly on long-context generation and instruction-following benchmarks.
background: Recent calibration sweeps showed persistent token-level degeneracies for specific attention heads and intermediate layers after FP8/INT8 quantization. Existing per-model rescale rules are brittle and require manual tuning for each new model variant. We need automated detection of layer/head outliers and local scale adjustments that preserve distributional properties while staying compatible with optimized kernels.
goal: Ship an automated workflow that: 1) detects per-layer and per-head activation outliers during calibration probes; 2) derives minimal additive/multiplicative rescale transforms that bring activations into quantizable range; 3) integrates transforms into quant profiles and runtime compatibility checks; 4) validate across LLama/Mistral/Qwen baselines with regression budgets <= 0.5% perplexity increase and <= 1 point drop on instruction-following metrics.
technical_approach: 1) Extend the calibration harness to emit per-layer activation histograms, headwise kurtosis/skew, and tail-percentile stats (99.9/99.99). 2) Implement a two-stage mitigation: (A) soft clipping using adaptive percentile-based thresholds with per-head scale factors, (B) local multiplicative rescale computed from rolling median absolute deviation (MAD) and robust variance estimator. 3) Add a constrained solver that minimizes L2 deviation from original activations subject to quantization dynamic range constraints to compute final layer transforms. 4) Produce canonical profile entries: transform type, parameters, and provenance metadata for runtime and tooling to apply or validate at serve-time. 5) Ensure transform representations are compatible with our kernel selection (no ops that break fused attention kernels).
calibration_workflow: 1) Baseline probe: run 10k tokens/1000 prompts per-model to collect activation stats for each tested sequence length (128, 512, 2048).
2) Identify candidate outlier buckets where tail > X * median (tunable threshold default 25).
3) Compute per-head soft-clip thresholds using 99.9/99.99 percentiles and derive multiplicative rescale via MAD to target effective dynamic range for FP8/INT8 formats.
4) Run constrained solver to produce smallest-magnitude transform that meets quant range constraints.
5) Re-run quantized model with transforms applied on an independent validation set to measure perplexity, EM/QA metrics, and instruction-following tasks.
6) Produce a candidate quant profile JSON with metadata and attach to review PR for model onboarding.
7) If candidates fail acceptance, back off to head-level clipping rather than global layer rescale and mark as 'requires manual review'.
validation_plan: Benchmarks: C4 perplexity (short+long contexts), HELM-style instruction-following subset, and internal regression suite of 120 prompts.
Pass criteria: <= 0.5% relative increase in perplexity on avg across testbeds, instruction-following drop <= 1 point, no severe token-looping cases observed in 1000 sampled completions.
Metrics to capture: delta_ppl, delta_exact_match, token_repeat_rate, headwise activation clipping fraction, runtime kernel fallback rate.
A/B rollout: Canary quant profile on Dedicated pool with 5% traffic before wide rollout; monitor error traces and latency impact.
Automated checks: CI step that runs the calibration harness and stores histograms; gating job fails if delta_ppl > 1.0% or token_repeat_rate regresses by >2x.
acceptance_criteria: Automated calibration harness emits per-layer/head stats and produces transform artifacts for LLama/Mistral/Qwen.
Quant profiles applied to FP8/INT8 variants meet validation pass criteria for at least two representative models (one LLama family, one Mistral/Qwen family).
Documentation and profile provenance: each profile includes calibration seed, probe corpus, and solver params.
Runtime compatibility tests: no regression in kernel selection for hot-path attention (fused kernels remain usable), and any fallback is flagged with reason.
Code review + tests merged and an internal demo notebook showing before/after samples for each model family.
Canary rollout executed and monitored for 72 hours with no critical incidents.
progress_updates: 2026-02-19: Spike completed to collect activation histograms for llama-2-13b and mistral-7b. Observed heavy-tailed activations in MLP post-FFN layers and narrow extreme spikes in attention outputs.
2026-02-25: Prototype soft-clip operator (percentile-based) implemented in calibration harness; initial runs reduce tail mass but introduce small bias in mean for some layers.
2026-03-01: Implemented MAD-based multiplicative rescale and constrained solver; end-to-end FP8 sim shows perplexity delta 0.8% on llama-2-13b (above target).
2026-03-05: Tuned thresholds and added head-priority heuristic (prefer clipping on low-importance heads); FP8 sim now 0.45% delta on LLama, 0.32% on Mistral, Qwen pending.
2026-03-09: Started Qwen-2 validation; observed attention head spikes due to rotary position embeddings—adjusted probe sequence lengths and improved solver constraints.
2026-03-10: Preparing PR with calibration artifacts and validation scripts; request review from @Sofia Chen (Applied ML) and @Noah Kim (Runtime).
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Rescales may break assumptions in fused attention kernels leading to kernel fallback and latency regressions. Mitigation: Constrain transforms to multiplicative factors within safe range and add a runtime compatibility check in profile generation.
Risk: Overfitting transforms to calibration corpus causing unseen regressions. Mitigation: Use cross-validation with multiple corpora and include conversation-style prompts in probes.
Risk: Solver introduces numeric instability for extremely small MAD values. Mitigation: Add regularization floor and fallback to percentile clipping for low-variance layers.

Risk: Operational complexity of per-head transforms increases profile size. Mitigation: Only persist transforms when they reduce validation delta; otherwise store as 'probe-only suggestion' in profile metadata.
notes: Prefer minimal-change transforms; human review required for any profile that changes more than 3 layers' scales by >1.5x.
If Qwen family requires structural edits (rotary-related), create follow-up ticket for embedding-aware probes.
Coordinate with console team to expose 'transform reason' in Rollouts dashboard for observability.
